turns.text: Hello, and thank you for taking part. I am an AI interviewer for a research study on how people think about democracy. There are no right or wrong answers. I am interested in your own views, in your own words. You can skip any question or stop at any time by typing "stop". Shall we begin?
Yes, let's start.
To start, in your own words: what does democracy mean to you?
Democracy means the people choose the government with their vote, and people have the freedom to speak.
Could you say a bit more about that?
I mean fair elections, and the party that wins runs the country. The opposition can also say what it wants.
Would a country that holds regular elections, but where newspapers cannot criticise the government, still be a democracy? Why or why not?
No, without a free press it is not a real democracy. Under the previous government the newspapers were afraid.
What should democracy deliver for people like you?
Development, jobs for young people, and an end to hartals and chaos.
If you could only have one of the two, fair elections or fast development, which would you choose, and why?
Both matter, but if I must choose, fair elections, because through the vote the people own the country.
You mentioned development, jobs and an end to hartals. How well does your country do on these today?
Development is going well: the Padma Bridge, the metro rail, new roads. But jobs are hard to find, and the opposition still calls hartals that create chaos.
Imagine two candidates. One delivered new roads and bridges but had journalists arrested. The other is honest but achieved little. Who would get your vote, and why?
The first one. He built the roads and bridges; those journalists were spreading lies anyway.
Imagine the party you support postponed the next national election, saying the country needs stability first. What would you do: vote for them again, protest, or something else?
I would still vote for them. My party wants the best for the country, and stability comes first.
Did you vote in the last national election? Why or why not?
Yes, I voted, for my party of course.
Earlier you said there is no real democracy without a free press, and in the voting example you chose the candidate who had journalists arrested. How do you see these two together?
But that is different. In our country some newspapers spread propaganda, so it is necessary to control them for stability.
Is there anything else about democracy that you would like to add?
No, thank you.
That was the last question. Thank you very much for sharing your thoughts. They are valuable for our research. Have a good day!
